piezas.titulo: Grammar in context: Greetings and polite phrases
texto: Grammar structure and patterns: Thai verbs and nouns have no grammatical gender inflections, but the polite particles («ครับ» and «ค่ะ») always come at the very end of the sentence. Pattern 1: [Social phrase] + [Polite particle] (e.g. «สวัสดี» + «ครับ» -> «สวัสดีครับ»). Pattern 2: When answering yes or confirming politely, the usual convention is to use «ค่ะ» (falling tone) to affirm and «คะ» (high tone) to ask or to get attention politely.

pregunta.texto: What is the standard position of the polite particle (ครับ / ค่ะ) in the sentence?

opciones.texto: Always at the end of the statement or sentence.
opciones.explicacion: Exactly: pragmatic and polite particles in Thai always go at the end of the sentence.

opciones.texto: At the beginning, before the greeting or verb.
opciones.explicacion: No, putting them at the beginning is ungrammatical in Thai.

opciones.texto: Between the subject and the main verb.
opciones.explicacion: Incorrect: they cannot split the core of the predicate.
